citation: Khasar SG, McCarter G, Levine JD. Epinephrine produces a beta-adrenergic receptor-mediated mechanical hyperalgesia and in vitro sensitization of rat nociceptors. J Neurophysiol 1999;81(3):1104-12
what_it_shows: The study the page's two-hour window comes from (reference 18 of Wang 2011). Epinephrine injected intradermally into the dorsum of the rat hindpaw produced mechanical hyperalgesia measured by the Randall-Selitto test; the hyperalgesia was dose-dependent, began within minutes and lasted two hours. It was blocked by a beta-adrenergic antagonist and not by an alpha-adrenergic antagonist, and epinephrine also sensitised cultured small-diameter dorsal root ganglion neurons in the absence of nerve injury. So the two-hour figure and the 'rat skin with no nerve damage' description are right, but the study was not run at one epinephrine amount.
quote_from_abstract: Intradermal injection of epinephrine, the major endogenous ligand for the beta-adrenergic receptor, into the dorsum of the hindpaw of the rat produced a dose-dependent mechanical hyperalgesia, quantified by the Randall-Selitto paw-withdrawal test.

citation: Khasar SG, Dina OA, Green PG, Levine JD. Sound stress-induced long-term enhancement of mechanical hyperalgesia in rats is maintained by sympathoadrenal catecholamines. J Pain 2009;10(10):1073-7
what_it_shows: Reference 17 of Wang 2011, and later Levine-group work on stress, catecholamines and pain. In rats, mechanical hyperalgesia persisted for up to 28 days after sound stress; removing the adrenal medulla abolished the enhancement of epinephrine-induced cutaneous and muscle hyperalgesia, and giving stress levels of epinephrine back to those rats restored it. It shows that epinephrine-dependent cutaneous hyperalgesia has been measured well beyond a two-hour window since 1999, though by sustained circulating epinephrine rather than by one injection into skin, so it does not by itself decide a claim scoped to epinephrine placed in skin.
quote_from_abstract: We present data showing mechanical hyperalgesia persisting for up to 28 days after exposure to sound stress, with evidence that the sympathoadrenal axis mediator epinephrine plays a major role.

citation: Dina OA, Aley KO, Isenberg W, Messing RO, Levine JD. Sex hormones regulate the contribution of PKCepsilon and PKA signalling in inflammatory pain in the rat. Eur J Neurosci 2001;13(12):2227-33
what_it_shows: Reference 4 of Wang 2011, which discusses it directly as the earlier account of the signalling routes for epinephrine-induced mechanical hyperalgesia. In rats and in PKCepsilon-knockout mice, epinephrine-induced mechanical hyperalgesia depended on PKCepsilon, PKA and nitric oxide synthase in males but not in normal females, and on MEK in both sexes; the pattern followed oestrogen. It is a further study since 1999 of epinephrine-induced mechanical hyperalgesia in skin, but it reports signalling rather than how long the hyperalgesia lasts or how that varies with the amount injected.
quote_from_abstract: In normal male but not female rats, epinephrine-induced mechanical hyperalgesia was antagonized by inhibitors of protein kinase Cepsilon (PKCepsilon), protein kinase A (PKA) and nitric oxide synthetase (NOS).

citation: Hucho TB, Dina OA, Levine JD. Epac mediates a cAMP-to-PKC signaling in inflammatory pain: an isolectin B4(+) neuron-specific mechanism. J Neurosci 2005;25(26):6119-26
what_it_shows: Reference 12 of Wang 2011, cited there both for beta2-adrenoceptors mediating epinephrine hyperalgesia in rats and for the Epac step in the cAMP-to-PKCepsilon route. It shows cAMP signalling to PKCepsilon through Epac, PLC and PLD in IB4-positive nociceptors, with mechanical hyperalgesia in a behavioural model. It is mechanism work on how nociceptors are sensitised rather than a measurement of how long a sensitisation window lasts.
quote_from_abstract: Also, in a behavioral model, cAMP produced mechanical hyperalgesia (tenderness) through Epac, PLC/PLD, and PKCepsilon.

citation: Khan MA, Gerner P, Wang GK. Amitriptyline for prolonged cutaneous analgesia in the rat. Anesthesiology 2002;96:109-16
what_it_shows: The rat cutaneous-analgesia model that Wang 2008 took its method from: a single subcutaneous injection into shaved dorsal skin, with the cutaneous trunci muscle reflex to pinprick scored quantitatively. It compares amitriptyline with bupivacaine, each with and without epinephrine, and reports time to complete recovery and area under the effect-time curve for each. It is a second animal study of prolonged cutaneous analgesia from one skin injection, and it measures only the reflex - no skin histology and no nerve-fibre counts.
quote_from_abstract: Rats were subcutaneously injected on shaved dorsal skin. … Inhibition of the cutaneous trunci muscle reflex was evaluated quantitatively by the fraction of times a total of six pinpricks applied to the marked area failed to elicit a nocifensive motor response compared with control responses.

citation: Simone DA, Nolano M, Johnson T, Wendelschafer-Crabb G, Kennedy WR. Intradermal injection of capsaicin in humans produces degeneration and subsequent reinnervation of epidermal nerve fibers: correlation with sensory function. J Neurosci 1998;18:8947-59
what_it_shows: Reference 16 of Wang 2008, and the source of its PGP9.5 method. A human study in which an intradermal injection was followed by quantified counts of PGP9.5-immunoreactive epidermal nerve fibres in skin biopsies at several times afterwards, showing near-complete degeneration and later partial reinnervation, tracked against sensory testing. The injected substance is capsaicin, not a local anaesthetic, so it does not match the claims' intervention; it does show that the measurement the claims call for has been made in human skin after an intradermal injection, and that the method is established.
quote_from_abstract: At various times after capsaicin injection, nerve fibers were visualized immunohistochemically in skin biopsies and were quantified.

citation: Khodorova AB, Strichartz GR. The addition of dilute epinephrine produces equieffectiveness of bupivacaine enantiomers for cutaneous analgesia in the rat. Anesth Analg 2000;91:410-6
what_it_shows: Reference 24 of Wang 2008 and the source of its statement about what epinephrine does on its own in skin. The same rat model - subcutaneous injection, nocifensive reflex to pinprick - applied to the two bupivacaine enantiomers with and without epinephrine, and to epinephrine on its own at several dilutions. Outcome is analgesia only; no skin histology and no nerve-fibre counts.
quote_from_abstract: As a model of infiltration anesthesia, inhibition of a nocifensive reflex by subcutaneous injection … was evaluated quantitatively by the fraction of times a pinprick failed to evoke a nocifensive motor response.

citation: Wang CF, Gerner P, Wang SY, Wang GK. Bulleyaconitine A isolated from aconitum plant displays long-acting local anesthetic properties in vitro and in vivo. Anesthesiology 2007;107:82-90
what_it_shows: The companion study by the same group, cited as reference 3: the same adjuvant injected at the rat sciatic notch rather than into skin, alone and with lidocaine or with epinephrine, with sensory and motor function followed to recovery. No skin histology and no nerve-fibre counts. Recorded for completeness because it is the paper Wang 2008 builds on and because it is a prolonged-duration adjuvant study.
quote_from_abstract: The authors examined (1) the effects of BLA on neuronal voltage-gated Na channels in vitro under the whole cell patch clamp configuration and (2) the sensory and motor functions of rat sciatic nerve after single BLA injections in vivo.

citation: Davenport RE, Porcelli RJ, Iacono VJ, Bonura CF, Mallis GI, Baer PN. Effects of anesthetics containing epinephrine on catecholamine levels during periodontal surgery. J Periodontol 1990;61(9):553-8. doi:10.1902/jop.1990.61.9.553
what_it_shows: Double-blind crossover trial in nine stable cardiovascular-disease patients during periodontal surgery, lidocaine with epinephrine versus plain lidocaine: plasma epinephrine rose within minutes of the epinephrine-containing injection with no significant change in heart rate or mean arterial pressure. Amount given not stated in the abstract. Not in Troullos's reference list (published later); found by a PubMed search prompted by this paper.
quote_from_abstract: Nine stable cardiovascular disease patients were evaluated in a double-blind cross-over trial during periodontal surgery using [dose figure omitted] or lidocaine alone. ... Despite these elevations in epinephrine, no significant changes in heart rate or mean arterial pressure were noted.

citation: Meechan JG. Plasma potassium changes in hypertensive patients undergoing oral surgery with local anesthetics containing epinephrine. Anesth Prog 1997;44(3):106-9. PMC2148929
what_it_shows: Fourteen patients under treatment for hypertension (two groups: non-potassium-sparing diuretics, nonselective beta-blockers) had blood pressure, heart rate and plasma potassium measured before and after an epinephrine-containing dental anaesthetic, at an amount above the conventional cardiac-patient limit; no significant between-group difference in blood pressure, a between-group difference in heart-rate change, and a potassium fall in the diuretic group. Not a trial of epinephrine against none. Not in Troullos's reference list; found by a PubMed search prompted by this paper.
quote_from_abstract: Blood pressure, heart rate, and plasma potassium concentration were measured before and 10 min following the injection of [dose figure omitted] in 14 patients receiving treatment for hypertension. ... No significant changes in systolic or diastolic blood pressures were detected between groups at 10 min.

citation: Klingenstroem P, Westermark L. Local effects of adrenaline and phenylalanyl-lysyl-vasopressin in local anaesthesia. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1963;7:131-7
what_it_shows: The authors' own earlier study, cited in the opening paragraph of S-686-44 as the source of the colour observation: skin colour after lidocaine with adrenaline compared with lidocaine with Octapressin (felypressin), in which central cyanosis appeared within the pale zone after adrenaline but not after felypressin. PubMed holds no abstract; indexed under Anesthesia Local, Epinephrine, Lidocaine, Felypressin, Vasopressins, Humans. This is the 1963 skin-colour study the open question asks about; the paper's own description of it is quoted in the S-686-44 card.

citation: Nordqvist P, Dhuner KG. Influence of local anaesthetics with vasoconstrictors upon circulation and metabolism. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1961;5:63-71
what_it_shows: Cited by S-686-44 for the statement that the body's oxygen consumption rises after subcutaneous adrenaline or noradrenaline in major local anaesthesia. PubMed holds no abstract; indexed under Oxygen, Blood Circulation, Anesthetics Local and Vasoconstrictor Agents. Relevant as an earlier measurement of circulation and metabolism after local anaesthetics with vasoconstrictors, though systemic rather than at the injection site.

citation: Montgomery H, Horwitz O. Oxygen tension of tissues by the polarographic method. I. Introduction: oxygen tension and blood flow of the skin of human extremities. J Clin Invest 1950;29:1120-30
what_it_shows: The polarographic method source cited by S-686-44; human skin tissue-oxygen tension and blood flow in the extremities. Establishes that skin tissue-oxygen tension was being measured in human limbs by this method from 1950, well before the studies the page treats as the start of this literature. Free full text in PMC (PMC436153); PubMed holds no abstract.

citation: Bunke J, Merdasa A, Stridh M, et al. Hyperspectral and laser speckle contrast imaging for monitoring the effect of epinephrine in local anesthetics in oculoplastic surgery. Ophthalmic Plast Reconstr Surg 2022;38:462-468
what_it_shows: A second human study by the Bunke group (the page already cites Bunke 2021): perfusion and oxygen saturation measured simultaneously in the eyelid skin of 9 patients after injection of lidocaine with epinephrine, by laser speckle contrast imaging and hyperspectral imaging. Adds a further human skin oxygen-saturation measurement after an epinephrine-containing local anaesthetic; the time course is minutes, not hours, so it does not change C084's verdict. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44's topic, not from its reference list.
quote_from_abstract: This is the first study to assess blood perfusion and oxygen saturation (sO 2 ) simultaneously in response to a local anesthetic containing epinephrine in human oculoplastic surgery.

citation: Korkushko OV, Lishnevskaia VIu. [Significance of changes in individual indicators on intravascular homeostasis in development of circulatory hypoxia in aging]. Adv Gerontol 2002;9:73-8
what_it_shows: A human study in 45 healthy subjects aged 60-74 that combined an intradermal epinephrine injection as a laser-Doppler functional test with polarographic measurement of oxygen saturation in subcutaneous tissue. The abstract does not state that the oxygen measurement was made at the intradermal epinephrine site, or over hours, so it does not decide C084's 'human wheal' element; it is the nearest record found in which a human intradermal epinephrine injection and a polarographic tissue-oxygen measurement appear in the same protocol. Russian-language. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44, not from its reference list. The cached abstract has the injected amount and concentration replaced by [dose figure omitted].
quote_from_abstract: Oxygen saturation of the subcutaneous fat fibers was studied by polarography.

citation: Prasetyono TOH, Nindita E. The safety of one-per-mil tumescent infiltration into tissue that has survived ischemia. Arch Plast Surg 2019;46:108-113
what_it_shows: A randomised animal experiment (40 rat groin flaps previously subjected to ischaemia) measuring transcutaneous oxygen tension before and after infiltration with an epinephrine-containing tumescent solution against saline and no-infiltration controls. Cutaneous oxygenation fell significantly after both the epinephrine-containing and the saline infiltration, and no flap showed necrosis. It is a before-and-after measurement, not a time course over hours, so it does not change C084; it supports rather than refutes C093, which says no study found tissue damage at this kind of dose. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44. The cached abstract has the oxygen-tension values replaced by [dose figure omitted].
quote_from_abstract: Transcutaneous oxygen tension (TcPO2) was measured before and after infiltration, and changes in TcPO2 were statistically analyzed using analysis of variance, the paired t-test, and the independent t-test.

citation: Olgart L, Gazelius B. Effects of adrenaline and felypressin (octapressin) on blood flow and sensory nerve activity in the tooth. Acta Odontol Scand 1977;35:69-75
what_it_shows: An animal study (cats) comparing a local anaesthetic with adrenaline against one with felypressin, measuring pulp blood flow by tracer washout and intradental sensory nerve activity in the same cavity. Adrenaline, alone or with lidocaine, nearly abolished pulp blood flow within minutes and both functions recovered in most cases only after three hours; felypressin inhibited neither. The same adrenaline-versus-felypressin contrast as S-686-44, in a different tissue, with a flow time course of hours. Dental pulp is not skin and the injection was supraperiosteal, so it does not decide any skin claim. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44. The cached abstract has the injected amounts and concentrations replaced by [dose figure omitted].
quote_from_abstract: In most cases there was a recovery of both functions after 3 hours.

citation: Klingenstrom P, Nylen B, Westermark L. Vasoconstrictors and experimental flaps. Acta Chir Scand 1966;131:187-92
what_it_shows: A later animal (rat) study by the same group, indexed under Epinephrine, Lidocaine, Vasopressins, Necrosis, Skin and Sodium Chloride: vasoconstrictors in experimental skin flaps with necrosis as an outcome. Directly on the topic of skin necrosis after injected local anaesthetic with a vasoconstrictor, but PubMed holds no abstract and the full text was not obtained, so it cannot decide C093 and no verdict is changed on it. Found by an author search prompted by S-686-44, not from its reference list.

citation: Norberg KA, Palmer B. Effects of noradrenaline and felypressin on cutaneous local blood flow after sympathetic denervation. A study on rats. Scand J Plast Reconstr Surg 1972;6:106-9
what_it_shows: An animal (rat) study of cutaneous local blood flow responses to noradrenaline and to felypressin after sympathetic denervation, measured by xenon clearance; indexed under Denervation, Drug Hypersensitivity, Sympathectomy, Skin and Regional Blood Flow. It is on the topic of denervation supersensitivity of skin vessels to catecholamines, which the Lidocaine With Epinephrine Wheals page reasons from and which C018 and C019 are about; it is animal work and not an alpha-2-selective agonist, so it changes neither verdict (C018 is already refuted on human evidence, C019 asks about the time course of alpha-2 supersensitivity). PubMed holds no abstract. Found by a PubMed search prompted by S-686-44.

citation: Klingenstrom P, Nylen B, Westermark L. Experimental and clinical investigations of the local vasoconstrictive effect of two new derivatives of pituitary posterior lobe hormones. Plast Reconstr Surg 1967;39:503-11
what_it_shows: The same group's follow-on experimental and clinical study of two further vasopressin derivatives as local vasoconstrictors, indexed under Cyanosis, Epinephrine, Lidocaine, Vasopressins and Skin Transplantation. It continues the adrenaline-versus-vasopressin-analogue comparison of S-686-44 with cyanosis among its indexed outcomes. PubMed holds no abstract and the full text was not obtained, so it decides nothing. Found by an author search prompted by S-686-44.

citation: Guay J. Methemoglobinemia related to local anesthetics: a summary of 242 episodes. Anesth Analg 2009;108(3):837–845. doi:10.1213/ane.0b013e318187c4b1
what_it_shows: A summary of all published episodes of local-anaesthetic methaemoglobinaemia found in PubMed. Its results give a figure for adults; its concluding sentence gives a lower general limit — the limit Schmittner 2010 adopts and attributes to it (reference 8). So Schmittner repeats Guay's own conclusion rather than contradicting it. Figures omitted.
quote_from_abstract: The purpose of this article is to summarize all episodes of local anesthetic-related methemoglobinemia found in the medical literature.

citation: Lindenblatt N, Belusa L, Tiefenbach B, Schareck W, Olbrisch RR. Prilocaine plasma levels and methemoglobinemia in patients undergoing tumescent liposuction involving less than [dose figure omitted]. Aesthetic Plast Surg 2004;28(6):435–440. doi:10.1007/s00266-004-0009-5
what_it_shows: Prospective series of 25 patients with plasma prilocaine and methaemoglobin measured for 4 h after tumescent liposuction with dilute prilocaine and epinephrine; methaemoglobin stayed low and no patient showed clinical signs; the authors draw a conclusion about the length of postoperative monitoring. It predates Guay 2009 and recommends no lower limit, so it does not belong among analyses arguing for a lower limit than Guay's (C071's current proposed wording); for C068 it is a further series at doses far above a wheal session.
quote_from_abstract: In 25 patients undergoing liposuction involving less than [dose figure omitted] prilocaine levels and methemoglobinemia were measured over 4 h postoperatively.
